Theme 053 · Signature directions

Editorial Data

A Swiss-style annual report come alive: warm paper, a visible 12-column hairline grid, giant monospaced numerals as the heroes, serif headlines and small-caps mono labels. Each frame is allowed exactly one accent colour, so the anomaly reads like a number circled in a financial newspaper.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Hairline grid — 12 columns of 80 px, 1.5 px lines at 7 % ink — always visible, never decorative
  • Masthead — mark + “ACME · PULSE REPORT” + issue number on a 3 px rule; the film reads as a publication
  • Hero numeral — JetBrains Mono 230–300 px, tight tracking; the number is the headline
  • Task strip — perforated vertical tape of chores scrolling in a loop; the active row takes the accent
  • Annotated chart — single ink line, dashed event rule, coral point with a leader line and margin note
  • Colophon close — double rule, centred lockup, three mono stats, one coral pill

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Mask rise — headline blocks rise 100 % through a rule-aligned mask, power4.out 0.5 s, landing on the downbeat
  • Counter tick — numerals step once per beat (0.5 s at 120 BPM) with steps(1) — no tweening, like a split-second ledger
  • Line draw + pin — chart stroke-dashoffset 100 → 0 over one bar (2 s, linear); the anomaly numeral scales 1.08 → 1 in 0.2 s on the next downbeat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Numbers are the product here, and editorial typography makes them feel audited and serious — ideal for buyers who distrust flashy AI promises. Risk: it can feel cold and static; keep strict beat-locked reveals so the page “prints” in rhythm, and never add a second accent colour to a frame.

Adapt to your product: Choose the one number your product changes (time saved, errors caught, cost avoided) and make it the hero numeral; the chart simply shows the before/after around the moment your product intervenes.

References: https://github.com/Financial-Times/chart-doctor/tree/main/visual-vocabulary (FT Visual Vocabulary: newsroom chart grammar) · https://www.printmag.com/featured/swiss-style-principles-typefaces-designers/ (Swiss Style grid and typographic principles) · https://posterhouse.org/exhibition/the-swiss-grid/ (The Swiss Grid exhibition)
